protocol.client: scripts/benchmark_serving.py (repo-chat, fixed source-code corpus without tiling)
protocol.prefix_isolation: unique cache_salt per request; model, expert caches, graphs and host pages remain warm
protocol.warmup: one 4,096+256 request after startup; PLE prefault completed before the first measured request
protocol.ttft_definition: request start to first SSE event containing output token IDs
protocol.input_rate_definition: input_tokens / ttft_seconds; includes scheduling and first-token work
protocol.decode_definition: tokens after first output chunk / time until final output chunk
protocol.validity: complete SSE, exact usage and output counts, length finish

release_image_validation.note: built with docker/Dockerfile from this release tree; launched with scripts/docker_serve.sh

headline.note: one request (release run 2): best decode run; its prefill is within 0.2% of the best prefill run

full_context_development_runs.note: 260,096+2,048 on the tested development image with the same runtime files (release differs only by the opt-in PLE prefault implementation; these runs used an external read-only prefault)
full_context_development_runs.pressure_cause: another job's download filled the page cache and pushed the GPU workers' host memory into swap

fresh_agent_screen.suite: LBX AgentBench v0.2 frozen harness, xhigh reasoning, 32 steps, 16,384 tokens/response, temperature 0
fresh_agent_screen.limits: selected tasks, not the 15-task suite; no quality-parity claim

limits: Decode depends on MTP acceptance (51-64% observed on this workload) and on host RAM headroom.
The whole 51.2 GB PLE table must stay resident; stop other memory-heavy jobs while serving.
Vision and two-client profiles were not re-validated on this runtime before publication.
Measurements are single requests; no confidence interval.
